sara_cs: Cedarcrest reported a sudden p99 spike on embeddings since ~09:10 UTC. Baseline p99 ~300ms, now seeing 3-4s for batch requests. They attached request IDs req-abc123, req-def456. No code changes on their side yet. Can SRE triage? :eyes:

tyler_sre: Looking. Which route/model and any sample payloads?

sara_cs: Route: /v1/embeddings (batch). Model: open-embed-1024. Tenant: cedarcrest-prod. Sample req req-abc123 was ~1000 items (~12k tokens). Our logs show heavy cache wait + dbpool throttle. Snippet:
```
[09:11:02] cache: miss key=cedarcrest:embed:prefix latency=1523ms
[09:11:02] dbpool: msg=throttle_wait ms=1203
```

tyler_sre: Hmm Redis latency + dbpool throttle. Alex, any infra alerts for cache nodes?

alex_infra: Seeing elevated latency on redis-cache-3 (us-west-2) starting 09:04. Spikes 1.2-1.8s, connected_clients ~1500, ops/s high, evicted_keys climbing. Quick `redis-cli -h redis-cache-3 info` shows:
```
used_memory: 26GB
connected_clients: 1523
instantaneous_ops_per_sec: 12000
evicted_keys: 483
latency: latest=1.45s
```
Also lots of LRU evictions — looks like a large batch thrashing shared cache. Likely a noisy tenant job.

deepa_success: Confirmed: Cedarcrest runs a nightly indexing job that batches embeddings. They started a big run ~09:05 with ~200k items. They've paused for now if we request.

tyler_sre: Proposed mitigations (quick, low-risk):
- Apply temporary per-tenant throttle for cedarcrest embeddings (cap qps to 20)
- Create a temporary per-tenant cache namespace or reservation so their large prefixes don't evict shared keys
- If available, route heavy batch keys to a dedicated cache node/pool or put them on a delayed worker
I'll take the throttle + cache reservation.

sara_cs: Please keep Cedarcrest informed. I messaged them to pause the job until we apply mitigations.

ops-bot: action_taken: applied rate limit cedarcrest-prod on embeddings.batch qps=20 ttl=24h by tyler_sre

tyler_sre: Done — rate limit applied. Also increased redis-cache-3 maxmemory from 30GB -> 36GB and adjusted eviction tuning to favor shared prefixes. Created a temporary per-tenant prefix cedarcrest:dedicated: and pointed large batch writes there. Monitoring now.

alex_infra: Added migration rule to move cedarcrest heavy keys to redis-cache-5 (dedicated pool) for 48h window. Warming new node.

deepa_success: Customer paused two cycles and agreed to throttle at their side. They accepted the dedicated cache as a short-term fix. :thumbsup:

sara_cs: Customer reports p99 dropped to ~420ms within ~10 minutes after throttle + cache move. They're relieved but asking about long-term options (Reserved Capacity / Dedicated). I'll loop in AM for sales + account ops.

tyler_sre: Follow-ups logged: INF-2974 for infra work (per-tenant QoS + cache reservation APIs). Recommend offering Dedicated capacity + cache reservation as durable fix for Cedarcrest. Suggest a short postmortem in #postmortems with timeline + mitigation playbook.

ops-bot: incident_state: mitigated, severity: P2, closed_by: tyler_sre, closed_ts: 2109880143

sara_cs: Thanks everyone — closing thread. :white_check_mark:
